title: Recall the line after a gap and after a changed order
outcomes: Recalls a five-ply forcing line after other items have intervened
Recognises a transposition into a prepared line and plays the prepared move
Tells a transposition that reaches a flexible position from one that reaches the prepared line, and does not schedule the flexible one

steps.text: In **Remember the forcing lines, understand the rest** you sorted lines into exact recall and understanding. Two skills follow. First, **recall after a gap**: a line you studied a minute ago proves little. Second, **a transposition**: the same position can arrive by another move order. Study one line now; you will be asked for it again after other items, and by another route.

steps.caption: Two Knights, after 6.Bb5+ c6: take, retreat, step away.

line.say: White takes the pawn on c6; this is the move to recall.
The bishop retreats to a safe square.
Black asks the knight on g5 a question.
The knight steps away from the h6 pawn and heads for f4.

claims.statement: 7.dxc6 is the engine's first choice (depth 16); every other move is more than 40 centipawns lower.
After the five moves the white knight stands on h3.

steps.text: **Why the gap is the point.** On the Drill page a right answer returns after 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 or 32 days; a miss returns tomorrow. The bet is that recall after a gap sticks better than rereading; this project has not tested that on you [H]. **Rule of thumb:** schedule only forcing lines. Next, a position reached by another order: ask whether it is your prepared one.

steps.prompt: Put one forcing line from your repertoire on the Drill page (My repertoire on the Openings page). Plan the gaps on paper; the app does the scheduling, not the transposition check.
